correspondence.component_scope: Selected eastward headward opening and its connection into the upper receiving river
correspondence.finding: The selected opening corresponds at corridor scale to the eastward Nacimiento or Destierro Primero channel in Gil's own aerial-photograph and field-based headwater map. The neighboring de los Remansos and Horqueta del Sauce branches are separately mapped and join the receiving drainage; their labels are not transferred to the selection. The historical IGN original also depicts the selected west-to-east opening and its downstream turn. No exact source point or naming-transition vertex is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper receiving river through Sierra de la Ventana and Saldungaray to the reservoir approach
correspondence.finding: The original topographic channel, valley, settlements and successive tributary joins correspond to the selected southeastward river. Gil's own drainage maps distinguish the receiving Sauce Grande from its upper tributaries, including San Bernardo, El Negro and the later eastern tributaries. These joins support the corridor without treating each tributary as part of the selected through-river.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern reservoir approach, Paso de las Piedras water passage and southern outlet
correspondence.finding: Gil's original figures 4.1 and 4.2 map the Sauce Grande entering the northern reservoir arm and the river continuing from its southern outlet, with an eastern side arm kept distinct. The selected passage is consistent with this reservoir-through-river corridor. The historical IGN mosaic instead depicts the older river valley and the Divisorio-side junction; it is not used to establish the reservoir water surface. Gil's prose identifies downstream flow as regulated.
correspondence.scope_limit: No present water level, dam release, inundation boundary or exact submerged centerline is established.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Embalse / Dique Paso de las Piedras

correspondence.component_scope: Downstream north–south plain corridor past the Cabildo-side valley, Coronel Falcón and Paso Mayor
correspondence.finding: The historical original repeatedly labels the Sauce Grande and depicts its continuous channel, bends and intermediate tributary junctions. The selected line follows this main valley, remaining distinct from the western Napostá Chico/Bajo Hondo drainage. Gil's original drainage maps connect the reservoir outlet to this middle corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southeastward and eastward river bend toward the western lake inlet
correspondence.finding: The original map follows the named river from the main road/rail corridor into its eastward coastal-plain bend and the western Laguna Sauce Grande approach. The lake inlet and surrounding depressions are corroborated by Gil's own whole-basin drainage maps. Nearby isolated lagoons are not inferred to be selected through-waterbodies.

correspondence.component_scope: West-to-east lake passage
correspondence.finding: The historical original directly labels Laguna del Sauce Grande and depicts entry from the west and an eastern outflow. Gil's figures 4.1 and 4.2 independently depict the same named standing-water body within the connected drainage. This supports the selected lake connector at corridor scale, not a river name assigned to the lake.
correspondence.scope_limit: Historical water extents and drainage mapping do not establish present lake level or continuous present discharge.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake outflow, Las Mostazas-side junction and eastward lower coastal river
correspondence.finding: Both successful originals map an eastward outlet river north of Monte Hermoso/Sauce Grande, with Las Mostazas joining from the north. The selected lower eastward approach is consistent at regional scale. The neighboring Zanjón-side drainage is not treated as the selected river.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected final southward passage across the coastal dune belt
correspondence.finding: The selected final segment turns south toward the coast west of the Sauce Grande outlet depicted by the historical IGN original and Gil's original drainage map. Those sources continue the river farther east before its coastal opening. They do not establish a watercourse along the complete selected southward dune crossing. The gap is a material terminal-connection issue, not a requirement for exact bank or endpoint registration.
correspondence.excluded_inference: No canal, former mouth, intermittent distributary, engineered cut or present natural-river outlet is inferred along the selected final crossing.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern opening and Bananeira corridor
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is in the Tamanduá/Bandeira–Queimados corridor. The original depicts the small local stream connections and the northeast-running watercourse labelled Riacho Bananeira, followed toward Cachoeira da Barra and Capim. This identifies a bounded opening corridor, not the natural headwater of the complete named river; the name is not assigned to every small feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Canindé continuation toward São Mateus
correspondence.finding: The mapped continuous corridor through Capim, Ipueira da Pedra and Monte Alegre carries the Rio Canindé label and proceeds toward the southwestern approach to the São Mateus/Canindé-town setting. The overlap of the two municipal sheets is inspected. A formal Bananeira–Canindé name-change boundary is not established.

correspondence.component_scope: São Mateus waterbody, Canindé urban link and selected northern continuation
correspondence.finding: The original visibly identifies Açude S. Mateus and depicts several urban/adjacent drainage branches, including the separate Juriti approach and a Canindé-labelled course north of town. It does not establish the complete selected passage through the waterbody/urban setting and the selected northeastern continuation back into the mapped northern Canindé reach. The issue is the continuous corridor and branch/waterbody connection, not exact bank or vertex agreement. Neither a nearby reservoir label nor a continuous model line supplies that missing connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Canindé toward Paramoti and reservoir approach
correspondence.finding: Repeated direct labels, bends and joins establish the mapped Canindé corridor through São Domingos and Paramoti, past the Siriema tributary setting and northward past Jacaré, Muquém, Jurema and Irapuá toward the southern reservoir arm. The two municipal sheets overlap in the Paramoti reach. The maps alone do not establish a separately named or current managed São Domingos impoundment; an uninspected inventory was not used to add one.

correspondence.component_scope: Açude Pentecoste entry, through-waterbody corridor and outlet
correspondence.finding: The Canindé channel is depicted entering the long southern arm near Irapuá/Ingá/Capivara. The connected reservoir extends through the Jardim/Mulungu setting into the main body labelled Açude Pentecoste and reaches the northwestern outlet at Pentecoste. The selected corridor crosses this waterbody and outlet; it is not renamed as an uninterrupted natural-river reach. No uninspected alternative reservoir name or present operating condition is adopted.

correspondence.component_scope: Pentecoste outlet, Curu junction and São Luís do Curu corridor
correspondence.finding: The reservoir outlet joins the wider west-arriving river corridor at Pentecoste and continues north through the floodplain. Curu labels, the separate Caxitoré join, São Luís do Curu town/road crossing and the continuation toward Capim correspond. The separate western Curu approach and Caxitoré tributary are contextual joins, not extra selected headward fragments.

correspondence.component_scope: Intermediate and lower Curu
correspondence.finding: The continuous labelled river/floodplain is followed from Capim past the Curral Grande/Cágado setting and Morim/Carnaúbas to Poço Doce and the lower bends. Adjoining-map overlaps close the regional corridor. Nearby lagoons, canals and tributaries are depicted separately and are not silently included as through-route components.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual coastal ending and Atlantic receiving water
correspondence.finding: The lower Curu continues through the bend beside Santa Rita and the Ponta Paracuru coastal setting into the labelled Atlantic. This is the inspected coastal terminal corridor, distinct from the nearby Lagamar/lagoons and other coastal streams. The model sea-extension is not treated as a surveyed mouth, a present shoreline, or proof of a particular tidal branch.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Rio Curu coastal mouth; Oceano Atlântico receiving water

correspondence.component_scope: Selected headward opening and first northern hook
correspondence.finding: The original lithological map depicts several separate upper streams in the Huancarca–Putaca–Picha Ragra setting and their southeast-going receiving corridor. Its northern detail was inspected. This reading did not securely distinguish the selected opening and its first hook from the adjacent headward feeders, or demonstrate that exact branch choice into the receiving channel at ordinary tributary/corridor scale. The report’s general source description and regional hydronyms do not resolve that branch correspondence.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Materially incomplete for the selected initial branch and join. This is a branch/connection question, not a demand to name every small tributary or match an exact vertex.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper receiving corridor past Pachapaqui, Huasta and Chiquián
correspondence.finding: Readable source-map hydrography follows the upper north–south valley past Pachapaqui and the Huasta/Chiquián setting. Successive side-stream entries and the southward receiving course are depicted; the river label is explicitly printed by Chiquián. The report records historical upper reach names Piscapaccha or Picharagra, Aquia and Chiquián, so these are not flattened into a uniform Pativilca scalar.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Upper receiving-valley correspondence supported; no claim that this closes the preceding unresolved opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Chiquián–Llamac/Achin–Llaclla canyon and Rapay junction
correspondence.finding: The map shows the selected southeast then southward canyon corridor east of Chiquián, the eastern Llamac/Achin tributary setting, the continuation by Llaclla and Canis, and the Rapay confluence farther south. The selected continuation remains on the north–south main valley rather than transferring upstream onto those eastern tributaries.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported at ordinary river-corridor and junction scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Gorgor confluence, westward turn and Cahua/Huanchay junction corridor
correspondence.finding: The original map depicts the Gorgor entering from the east near the pronounced westward main-valley turn. The selected continuation follows the receiving channel west and southwest past the Cahua setting and the Huanchay tributary junction. This direction change is also described in the study’s dedicated river account.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported at ordinary main-valley and junction scale. The report mentions Cahua hydropower, but this does not establish a selected tunnel, canal or reservoir crossing.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower valley through Alpas/Cochas and the Pativilca–Barranca coastal approach
correspondence.finding: Continuous mapped river hydrography leads west through the lower valley past Alpas/Cochas and the Araya/Huayto–Vinto setting, then southwest near Pativilca. The main river is distinguished from adjacent quebradas and the separately labelled acequia near the coastal plain.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported at generalized lower-river corridor scale; current irrigation operations and exact braid selection are unverified.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual Pacific terminal near Malvarrosa/Barranca
correspondence.finding: The river is visibly drawn to the coastline below the Piedra Blanca/La Garita setting, north of Barranca. The dedicated report account identifies the mouth at Malvarrosa–Barranca in the Pacific. This supports the actual coastal outlet rather than stopping at the inland lower-river label.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Historical river-to-Pacific connection supported; present shoreline and exact mouth vertex not asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake, reservoir and managed-connector scope
correspondence.finding: No lake or reservoir passage is identified on the supported selected main-valley corridor in the inspected map. The study describes glacial lakes elsewhere in the catchment and Cahua hydropower, but these do not establish any selected lake crossing or managed connector. correspondence.coverage_limit: No positive selected lake/reservoir/managed passage established; unresolved opening remains included in the primary material gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward opening and northern inland-ice corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected opening, initial southwestward passage and extended southward interval fall within the original national map’s Inland Ice coverage. All lie north of the regional Sheet 1 northern neatline and are covered by the national map; they are not omitted or attributed to the regional map.
correspondence.feature_type_limit: The national map’s surface contours, ice-thickness isopachs, sub-ice bedrock contours and aeromagnetic lineaments are not mapped river traces.

correspondence.component_scope: National/regional overlap and southern inland-ice corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected path enters the regional sheet across its 62°30′N edge in mapped ice, with continuous source-area overlap from the national original. The subsequent southward corridor is fully visible in the regional map’s ice field down toward the exposed-rock margin.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southward-to-westward turn and approach to fragment junction
correspondence.finding: The complete lower turn is within readable regional coverage of the irregular ice/bedrock margin and exposed-rock outcrops east of the inner Sermilik setting. The selected passage is geographically accounted for; the cartography does not establish a river through the ice and rock or a hydraulic join.

correspondence.component_scope: Fragment junction and complete short western terminal fragment
correspondence.finding: The entire selected fragment, including its eastern junction with FID 8914, slight northward bend and final western ending, is visible within the regional map’s ice/rock-margin and inner coastal setting. No part is omitted merely because its pack stage differs from FID 8914.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected terminal correspondence
correspondence.finding: The final selected point corresponds at the source scale to the historical ice-front/fjord-head setting at the inner end of the water body labelled Sermilik. It is not established as an ordinary river mouth. The nearby mapped glacier labels are not assigned to this whole modeled object.
correspondence.name_scope: Fjord context only, not a selected natural-river or glacier name.
